summary.title: Lessons from Keith Rabois Essay 2: How to Interview an Executive
summary.one_liner: You learn a five-trait framework for interviewing executives, including how to tell value-creating roles from value-protecting ones and how to test ownership mentality, strategic thinking, fit, and talent magnetism.
keywords: value creating vs value protecting roles
what would you do differently as ceo
takeaways: First decide whether an executive role is value creating (accept risk, hire ambitious people) or value protecting (hire proven, zero-defect experts).
Test ownership by asking what they would have done differently as CEO at their last company, and listen for "we" and "I" rather than "they".
Assess strategic thinking by seeing whether candidates ask questions that probe the business equation and reveal levers you had not considered.
Match candidate strengths to the biggest gaps between company risks and current leadership strengths, and check that they bring diverse workstyles.
Spend 15-20 hours working with candidates, and use reference calls to check whether they build and retain strong teams.
summary.summary:
This essay by Keith Rabois explains how a CEO should interview executives, which differs from interviewing individual contributors. It sets out five traits to assess: whether the role creates or protects value, ownership mentality, strategic thinking, alignment with company risks and diversity of style, and talent magnetism. The author illustrates the points with examples from Stripe, a local marketplace startup, Teespring and Affirm, including sample Q&A about business levers. It closes with practical advice on real work tests, reference checks and hiring plans.</summary>
